label: lower after a1 / a1->S2 trials; higher after reward (D1) and at S2 (D2)
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1)*(prev_action==1)*(prev_state==2) ;; (phase == GO)*(prev_action==1)*(prev_state==2) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2)*(prev_action==1)*(prev_state==2)*(prev_reward==0) ;; (phase == D1) * choice ;; (phase == D2)*(prev_state==2)*(prev_reward==0)
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 9 is near 0.9 early and decays strongly over the episode (timing R^2 0.86). Beyond timing: at D1 it is lower after an a1 choice (about -0.02), further lower when a1 led to S2 (rare, about -0.04), higher after a rewarded trial (+0.045), and lower when the policy favours a1 (negative weight on choice logit). At GO it is lower after a1->S2 trials (-0.04). At D2 it is higher when the reached state is S2 (+0.05) and lower after an unrewarded S2 trial (-0.05), more so after a1 S2 u. All terms observed (choice = model policy logit). Test R^2 beyond timing 0.55 vs all ceiling 0.64 (86%). Residual misses are mostly late-episode (trials 85-99) runs of a1 S1 choices where the gate is lower than predicted; multiplicative late-episode scaling did not help. Trial-before terms added little (<0.01).

issues: Reproduced: the 8 terms score test R^2 beyond timing 0.5505 against an 'all' ceiling of 0.64 (86%). The fitted weights match the explanation: D1 prev_a1 -0.023, D1 prev_reward +0.045, D1 a1->S2 -0.041, GO a1->S2 -0.038, D2 state S2 +0.054, D2 a1S2u -0.028 on top of D2 prevS2u -0.047, D1 choice -0.010.

Overstated wording: the explanation says every term uses only what the agent has seen, but the D1 choice logit is a model-output cue, which the tool's 'all observed' reference leaves out. Dropping that one term cuts test R^2 to 0.468 (vs 0.59 observed ceiling, ~79%), so about 0.08 of the score comes from the policy logit. That is the agent's own computed quantity, not a future variable, but the label should say so.

The D1 choice term mostly stands in for the agent's upcoming choice. Using the future (phase==D1)*(action==1) instead gives 0.526, close to the logit's 0.550. Since the observed-only logit does at least as well, using it is legitimate.

The '+ after reward at D1' claim is less clean than it sounds. The D1 residual table shows reward and choice interact: a1 S2 u -0.129, a1 S1 u -0.075, a1 S2 r -0.052, a1 S1 r -0.019, a2 r +0.06. In practice the drop after an a1 choice is mostly a drop after an unrewarded a1 trial. Even so, a (prev_a1 & unrewarded) term gives the same 0.546, so it makes little difference.

Misses: the worst windows are late-episode (t87-99) runs of a1->S1 choices, where the actual value is about 0.2 below the prediction at every phase. Mean errors by phase x previous trial stay small (|err| <= 0.028; GO slightly under-predicted at +0.013 on average). None of these fixed it: terms scaled by exp(ep_trial/15) (0.41-0.52), late x prev_a1, late x choice, two a1 trials in a row, value, or the hidden good state as an 8th term (all <= 0.541). This looks like late-episode variance that grows with time and that the cue set cannot capture, not a missed systematic class.
I could not beat the claimed terms with alternatives: full per-phase last-trial tables plus choice in every phase scored 0.498 and 0.541.
